keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Gajaaga row). The kingdom "sat on the upper Senegal River, mainly in present-day Senegal with some parts of Mali" and "controlled both banks from the Kayes area downstream to Bakel". The infobox says the Bacili dynasty was founded before 1000 CE; the body says the dynasty arrived between the 8th and 11th centuries and its control was "only truly cemented in the 13th century". The page gives no outline.

region.text: Gajaaga on both banks of the upper Senegal from the Kayes area downstream to Bakel (the river widened by 40 km, cut to that stretch; the page gives no outline)

ledger.note: Before 1000: the kingdom exists. Infobox: Bacili dynasty founded before 1000 CE ("only truly cemented in the 13th century" in the body); 1000 is a bridging year for the page's "before 1000 CE". Gajaaga was a vassal of Jolof and Takrur (undated) and a nominal tributary of Futa Toro from the late 16th century (suzerains' ledgers).

region.text: Bundu, the Falémé-Gambia plateau 'between 13 and 15 degrees north and 12 and 13 degrees west' (the bundu dossier's box), once 'a sparsely populated part of the kingdom of Gajaaga'

ledger.note: 1690: Bundu is carved from Gajaaga. "Fula cleric Malick Sy arrived in 1690, and the tunka gave him control over a town and later the wider Bundu area"; "in the 18th century Bundu grew stronger as Gajaaga declined".

region.text: Bakel and its fort on the upper Senegal ('In 1855 he annexed Bakel and Medine, where he built another fort'; Medine lies in Khasso, not Gajaaga)

ledger.note: 1855: Bakel is annexed. "1855: Bakel and Medine were annexed" (Gajaaga page; Medine lies in Khasso, not Gajaaga); the French had re-established a fort at Bakel in 1820. In 1844 separate treaties with the leaders of Gooy and Kamera recognised their de facto separation. [Reviewer af-03-x, 2026-10-19: region narrowed from the whole kingdom to Bakel, the only Gajaaga town the page says was annexed in 1855; the whole kingdom ends in 1858.]

notes:
Gajaaga (Galam), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Gajaaga (one page).

The start is a bridge: the page says "before 1000 CE" (infobox), with a dynasty arrival between the 8th and 11th centuries and control "only truly cemented in the 13th century"; the ghana-empire dossier (Wagadu) may claim the same river lands in the first centuries. The Bundu split (1690, Malick Sy) is paired with the bundu dossier's found. The 1844 treaties with the leaders of Gooy and Kamera recognise a de facto split into two states; the page gives no further boundary. The page says Medine was annexed in 1855, but Medine is in Khasso; the loss of 1855 is drawn over Gajaaga whole. The Futa Toro tribute from the late 16th century belongs in the futa-toro ledger (it carries Gajaaga among the tributaries since 1599).
Gazetteer: Makhaana (Kamera), Tiyabu (Gooy), Bakel, Medine.
